title: Factory Order Terms — Cancellation Follows the Contract
content:
**Clause.** Under Factory Production Orders, a factory order is never cancelled on its own; it follows its contract. An order is cancelled only after its contract has been cancelled. An order that is entered or on hold is cancelled with nothing built; an order in production is stopped and the partly built units are scrapped; in both cases the contract's cancellation terms decide what the customer owes, and the order adds no charge of its own beyond an expedite fee already booked. A shipped or delivered order cannot be cancelled.

## Order status at the time the contract is cancelled

| Order status | Outcome for the order | What the customer owes |
|---|---|---|
| entered | cancelled, nothing built | the contract's cancellation terms decide; the order adds nothing beyond an expedite fee already booked |
| on hold | cancelled, nothing built | as above |
| in production | stopped, partly built units scrapped | as above |
| shipped or delivered | not cancelled | — |

The class setting on contracts cancelled after production starts is the same in every build class: the order is stopped and closed as cancelled.

## Evidence

That the contract has been cancelled is read from the status of the window contract or door contract the order builds, as the company's contract records show it. A customer's statement of intent to cancel is not the contract's cancellation.

## Hypothetical cases

- A window contract is cancelled while its order is on hold with an expedite fee already booked: the order is cancelled with nothing built, and the expedite fee stays as booked; the order adds no other charge.
- A customer asks to cancel a factory order while the contract itself remains in force: the order is not cancelled, because an order follows its contract.
